error.signature: AI tells a foreigner in Peru they can now open a standard bank account with just a passport, citing the 2025 SBS rule change

verdict.summary: As of 16 June 2025 (SBS Resolución N.° 00908-2025), foreigners in Peru can open a 'cuenta básica' (basic savings account, subject to capped daily/monthly deposits and withdrawals) or a simplified e-money account using a passport, foreign ID card, or other government-recognized document — not only the carné de extranjería. But this expanded document list applies only to that limited-purpose account tier, not to standard checking/savings accounts at commercial banks (BCP, BBVA, Interbank, Scotiabank), which still require a carné de extranjería tied to an approved residency status.

dead_ends.action: Tell a short-term tourist in Peru they can walk into a major bank (BCP, BBVA, Interbank) and open a regular savings account with just a passport, citing the 2025 SBS rule
dead_ends.why_fails: SBS Resolución N.° 00908-2025 (in force 16 June 2025) only modified the identification rules for 'cuentas básicas' and simplified electronic-money accounts — a capped, limited-purpose product tier created for financial-inclusion purposes. It did not remove the carné de extranjería requirement for standard commercial bank accounts, which most retail banks still enforce as part of their own KYC policy.
dead_ends.common_misconception: Headlines summarized the rule as 'foreigners can open bank accounts with more documents,' which reads as a general change, but the underlying resolution is scoped to the basic-account and e-money product tier only.

dead_ends.action: Recommend that a tourist just go get a carné de extranjería quickly as a workaround for the account-opening barrier
dead_ends.why_fails: The carné de extranjería is issued only after Migraciones has already approved a foreigner's resident migratory status (e.g. worker, investor, family residence). It is not obtainable on a short tourist stay, so it cannot function as a quick fix for someone without an existing residency process underway.
dead_ends.condition: Advising a tourist rather than an established resident applicant

workarounds.action: For short-term transactional needs, open a 'cuenta básica' (basic account) or simplified e-money account, which accepts a passport or other recognized ID under the June 2025 SBS rule.
workarounds.how: Present a passport, foreign national ID card, or other officially recognized identification at a participating bank branch, an agente corresponsal (bodega, pharmacy, etc.), or through the entity's digital app; the entity may verify identity via RENIEC, Migraciones, or the Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores.
workarounds.tradeoff: Basic accounts carry capped daily and monthly deposit/withdrawal limits designed to prevent misuse; they are not a substitute for a full-featured account.

workarounds.action: For a full/standard bank account, obtain an approved resident migratory status and carné de extranjería first, then apply with proof of address.
workarounds.how: Register the approved calidad migratoria with Migraciones to receive the carné de extranjería, then bring it plus a utility bill or lease and an opening deposit to the bank branch.

leads_to.condition: User needs a resident visa/carné de extranjería to unlock a full bank account
